Adding one is a deliberate act and shows up in the diff. Never list a control that posts, votes, edits or deletes.

_iframeIsViewportCapped: 🔴 MEASURED 2026-09-27 ON LIVE 0.4.7, AND IT CORRECTS A CLAIM THIS FILE USED TO MAKE. On the `/apps/run/<slug>` full-page surface the host does NOT fit the iframe to content. The iframe carries inline `flex: 1 1 0%` inside a flex parent with `overflow: hidden`, so it is sized to the REMAINING VIEWPORT HEIGHT and the app's overflow is clipped by the parent. Measured at three emulated viewport heights (CSS 900 / 1100 / 1400): iframe height 752 / 952 / 1253, while the app's own content height stayed 2166 / 2166 / 2168. The host page itself does NOT scroll at any of them (documentElement.scrollHeight == innerHeight, overflow hidden). ── 🔴 THE CONSEQUENCE THAT DECIDES THIS RECIPE'S SHAPE: `section-matchups` (CSS 1175..1482) and `section-prompts` (CSS 1500..2142) are BELOW the iframe's visible lower edge at ALL THREE heights, and no window size reaches them — at the tallest of the three the iframe is still only 1253. THOSE TWO SECTIONS ARE UNPHOTOGRAPHABLE BY THIS PIPELINE. The store listing can no longer show a matchups view or a prompts view at all; it can show the grid, and the three overlays this recipe captures. That is a real loss against the old tabbed IA and it is not a framing problem — say so rather than shipping a recipe that implies otherwise. ── ⚠️ AND IT RETIRES ONE OF THE TWO RECORDED REASONS SCROLLING WAS REFUSED. The note that stood here claimed the app 'has no in-iframe scroll at all' because `useBlockResize(rootRef)` makes the host fit the iframe to content, so reaching a lower section would scroll the HOST page and `frame.py` would refuse it as `crop_rect_outside`. 🔴 THAT MECHANISM IS FALSE ON 0.4.7, measured not inferred: the app frame's own document scrolls (`window.scrollTo(0,800)` inside the frame moved `scrollY` to 800.44, documentElement.clientHeight 952 against scrollHeight 2166), and the host page does not move, so no negative top gap arises and `crop_rect_outside` would never fire for that reason. ✅ THE OTHER REASON STANDS AND IS THE ONLY ONE THAT MATTERS: `KNOWN_ACTIONS` in `plan.py` is click / clickIfPresent / type / key / waitForText / waitForGone / trustedKey / sleep / nav — re-read 2026-09-27, there is still NO `scroll` verb, and an unknown verb is REFUSED (`bad_recipe`), never skipped. Adding one is a change to `plan.py` plus `capture.sh` plus the bridge op plus the mutation battery, and it was explicitly out of scope for this pass. 🔴 DO NOT TREAT THE CORRECTION ABOVE AS PERMISSION TO BUILD THE SCROLL ROUTE — it is recorded so the next reader argues from what is true, and the decision to add a verb belongs to whoever owns this skill. Note also that a `scroll` verb now looks CHEAPER than the old note implied, because an in-iframe scroll leaves the app frame's rect untouched and `yFrom: appFrame` would survive it; that is an argument to be made deliberately, not a licence.
_viewportOfRecord: 🔴 RE-RUNNING THIS RECIPE DOES NOT REQUIRE THE OPERATOR'S WINDOW TO BE THE ONE crop._measuredGeometry NAMES — EMULATE THE VIEWPORT INSTEAD. Measured 2026-09-08 and RE-CONFIRMED 2026-09-27 against 0.4.7: the emulation below reproduces the probe answer APPFRAME_RECT:104,64,-1,1709,1255,0 exactly, so `viewport_of_record` is satisfied without touching the operator's screen. 🔴 THE TRAP IS THAT TWO GATES READ DIFFERENT UNITS AND SATISFYING ONE BREAKS THE OTHER. `viewport_of_record` compares crop._measuredGeometry.viewport (1709x1255) against the CAPTURE's pixel dimensions; `app_frame_scale` compares the PROBE's reading, which is CSS px x devicePixelRatio, against that same capture. The operator's display here has DPR 1.140625, and `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` does NOT make window.devicePixelRatio return the overridden deviceScaleFactor — measured: emulating 1709x1255 at --dsf 1 satisfied viewport_of_record and then died on app_frame_scale reporting a 1950x1431 page against a 1709x1255 capture (1709 x 1.140625 = 1950). ✅ THE SPELLING THAT WORKS: emulate in CSS px and let the scale factor carry the DPR, so both readings land on 1709x1255 — `browser --instance work --tab <id> emulate --width 1498 --height 1100 --dsf 1.140625` (1498 x 1.140625 = 1708.7 -> 1709; 1100 x 1.140625 = 1254.7 -> 1255; the gates' tolerance is 2px). Then `capture.sh <recipe> --instance work --tab <id> --no-foreground`. 🔴 `--no-foreground` IS LOAD-BEARING HERE, NOT DIAGNOSTICS: an ACTIVE tab is captured by captureVisibleTab, which photographs real window pixels and IGNORES the emulation, so foregrounding silently re-introduces the mismatch. A tab opened by `browser open` is created inactive, which is what routes the capture onto CDP — and CDP honours the override. Confirm with `"via": "cdp"` in the screenshot op's answer. ⚠️ DERIVE --dsf FROM THE LIVE DISPLAY, DO NOT COPY 1.140625 — it is this operator's monitor today, not a constant; read devicePixelRatio and divide the recorded viewport by it. (2026-09-27: re-derived live, still 1.140625 on a single 3440x1440 DP-0.) ⚠️ It also does NOT rescue the horizontal anchor: the live probe still answers leftInset=0 rightGap=-1, so this app IS still full-bleed and `xFrom`/`wFrom` remain ruled out for it — do not spend a session on that conversion. ✅ Evidence the y-anchor is earning its keep: appFrameTop moved 141 -> 104 between the 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-08 readings and `yFrom: appFrame` absorbed it with no edit; it read 104 again on 2026-09-27.

Drive a browser for those. ── 🔴 THE THREE STATES ARE NOW OVERLAYS, NOT PANELS, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE DISCRIMINATORS WORK AGAIN. Each state clicks one trigger and waits on text only the overlay it opens renders. The three overlays are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — measured, one open at a time, opening one closes the others — so a mis-click cannot satisfy the wrong state's wait. See `_discriminators` for the presence matrix, which is the mechanical check that replaces the inert waits 0.4.7 broke. ── 🔴 WHY NOT A SCROLL TO EACH SECTION: `_iframeIsViewportCapped`. Two sections are unreachable at any window size and there is no `scroll` verb. Read that note before proposing a fix. ── 🔴 KEPT FROM THE OLD NOTE BECAUSE THE PRINCIPLE OUTLIVED ITS SELECTORS: every state must wait on something only the state it intends renders, so a drifted selector FAILS the run instead of silently capturing the wrong screen. The old form waited on panel-BODY text, which was right while exactly one panel mounted at a time and went INERT the moment all three sections mounted together. The replacement is not a better wording of the same idea — it is a different anchor (an overlay that exists in one state only), which is why it cannot rot the same way. Do not 'simplify' these waits back onto section text.
_discriminators:
🔴 THE MEASURED PRESENCE MATRIX — THIS IS THE CHECK, NOT THE PROSE ABOVE. `waitForText` is a SUBSTRING MATCH over the bridge `text` op's whole-frame output, and that output is DOM text, so it includes the two sections that are clipped out of sight. That is exactly why the old discriminators went inert. Measured 2026-09-27 against live 0.4.7, four reads (base + one per overlay), each string tested as a substring of each read:
  'Build a grid'              base - | contribute PRESENT | matchup -       | prompt -        -> UNIQUE
  'Matchup'                   base - | contribute -       | matchup PRESENT | prompt -        -> UNIQUE
  'Default (every ecosystem)' base - | contribute -       | matchup -       | prompt PRESENT  -> UNIQUE
and the three the recipe used to carry, on the SAME reads:
  'Submit and vote on checkpoint'  PRESENT in all four
  'Submit and vote on prompts'     PRESENT in all four
  'Top Grid'                       PRESENT in all four
CONTROLS: an absent sentinel ('ZZZ-absent-sentinel') returned absent in all four, and 'Model Benchmarking' returned present in all four — so the check can report both values and the three zeros above are not a broken matcher. ── 🔴 THE WEAKEST LINK IS 'Matchup' AND IT IS FLAGGED ON PURPOSE. It is a single common word and it is unique only BY CASE: the base read contains 'matchups x prompts' (lower) and '2 MATCHUPS x 5 PROMPTS' (upper), and the detail panel's own title 'Matchup' (title case) is the only title-case occurrence. If any future version renders a title-case 'Matchups' heading anywhere on the page, this discriminator goes INERT SILENTLY — the same failure the 0.4.7 IA caused, in a new spelling. It survives only because the panel title is structural chrome rather than data; every other string inside `matchup-detail` is either dataset ('Illustrious v9.0', 'DreamShaper', the LoRA name) or shared with the clipped sections ('INCLUDED', 'CONFIGS', 'Edit', 'Remove'). 🔴 RE-RUN THIS MATRIX, DO NOT TRUST IT: open each overlay, take the frame `text`, and check each string against all four reads. A discriminator that has stopped discriminating looks identical to one that works — three identical screenshots and exit 0. ── Why NOT a testid: `plan.py` emits `waitForText` as the `text` op with EMPTY argv, so the output is plain text with no attributes and a testid can never match. Selecting on the overlay's own `data-testid` would be the structurally better guard and the recipe form cannot express it.

ready._comment: 🔴 RE-POINTED 2026-09-27. This was `view-switch`, the tab strip, which 0.4.7 DELETED — and because `ready` is the BOOT GATE rather than a click step, that failure arrived as a full 45s stall with NO action attempted, which reads like a dead app rather than a drifted selector. The recipe's own notes record that this precise misdiagnosis already cost a session once, which is why it is called out here again. `section-grids` replaces it and was verified PRESENT AT BOOT, not merely eventually: after a `nav` to the app URL, a poll of the app frame at +2s through +12s found `section-grids`, `results-grid`, `contribute-trigger`, `grid-group-matchup` and `grid-col-header` all present at EVERY sample, and `app-loading` absent at every sample (it had already resolved before the first read). 🔴 THE GATE IS DELIBERATELY THE SECTION AND NOT `app-content`: `app-content` is the app's outer shell and would go true before the grid exists, which is the too-early gate this mechanism exists to prevent — a click fired into a still-booting app is discarded and the NEXT wait times out naming the wrong control. `section-grids` is the container all three of this recipe's triggers live inside, so if it is present the triggers are reachable. `loadingTestid` is `app-loading`, which the served bundle carries (count 1); it was never observed true from here, so it is declared on the bundle's evidence and not on an observation of the loading state itself.

_howToDismissal: 🔴 THE FIRST ACTION OF EVERY STATE IS PROFILE-DEPENDENT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS `clickIfPresent` AND NOT `click`. Dismissing the how-to PERSISTS across reloads (see `_noExplainerState`), so `[data-testid='howto-dismiss']` exists on a profile that has never run this app and is ABSENT on every profile that has. Re-measured 2026-09-27 on live 0.4.7: `howto-dismiss` is present in the served bundle (count 1) and ABSENT from the live DOM on this operator's profile, and the string 'How this works' is likewise in the bundle but not in the rendered text — so on this profile the `clickIfPresent` skips and the `waitForGone` is satisfied instantly. Both are correct, and neither may be the only supported one: deleting the click breaks a fresh profile, while leaving it a plain `click` makes the bridge's `element_not_found` an action FAILURE on a used one. The `waitForGone` that follows is NOT dead and must stay: a wait-until-absent is satisfied instantly when the panel is already gone, and on a fresh profile it is the only thing stopping the next click from racing the dismissal. ⚠️ It is therefore VACUOUS on this profile — it proves nothing here, and that is not a reason to delete it.

_mutualExclusion: 🔴 EVERY STATE ASSERTS ITS OWN OVERLAY IS OPEN *AND* THAT THE OTHER TWO ARE CLOSED, AND THE SECOND HALF IS NOT SYMMETRY FOR ITS OWN SAKE — IT IS A DEFECT THAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED INTO AN ASSET ON 2026-09-27 AND WAS CAUGHT BY EYE, NOT BY A GATE. THE INCIDENT: a full run exited 0, passed store-bounds, and produced a `grid-contribute` asset showing the Contribute dropdown AND a leftover Prompt detail panel open together. The single `waitForText` was satisfied — 'Build a grid' really was on screen — so nothing in the pipeline objected. ── THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL: `capture.sh` reloads the app before every state EXCEPT THE FIRST ('the first state already landed'), so state 1 inherits whatever the tab was left in. Here the tab had been driven by hand while the recipe was being authored and was sitting on an open `prompt-detail`. Any run that passes `--tab <id>` of a tab someone has been clicking in is exposed; a tab `capture.sh` opens itself is not. 🔴 AND THE MUTUAL EXCLUSION I HAD MEASURED WAS TOO NARROW A READING: opening one DETAIL panel does close the other (`grid-group-matchup` then `grid-col-header` leaves exactly one), but the CONTRIBUTE MENU is a separate dropdown that happily coexists with a detail panel. 'They are mutually exclusive' was true of the pair I tested and false of the pair I did not. ── WHY THE GUARD IS RIGHT RATHER THAN A WORKAROUND: it pins a RELATIONSHIP (this overlay open, those two closed) instead of a single word, so it fails LOUDLY — `waitForGone` polls until absent and then times out as an action failure (exit 4) naming the string — rather than silently photographing two overlays. It does NOT repair a dirty tab and is not meant to; it converts a silent wrong-screen capture into a stopped run. ⚠️ IT IS VACUOUS ON A CLEAN RUN, which is exactly why it must not be deleted as dead weight: on states 2 and 3 the reload has already guaranteed the condition, and on state 1 it is the only thing standing between a dirty tab and a shipped asset. ✅ WATCHED FAILING BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED: re-running the contaminated setup (prompt-detail left open, then the grid-contribute state) fails on `waitForGone 'Default (every ecosystem)'` with exit 4 and ships no asset, where the pre-guard recipe exited 0 and shipped the double-overlay image.
_statesRebuilt: 🔴 THE STATE SET CHANGED SHAPE ON 2026-09-27, not just its selectors. It was three TAB PANELS (matchups / prompts / grid); it is now three OVERLAYS opened from the grid. That was forced, not preferred: `_iframeIsViewportCapped` shows the matchups and prompts sections sit below the iframe's visible lower edge at every window size, so the two states that used to photograph them cannot be photographed at all. ── ✅ WHY OVERLAYS WORK, MEASURED IN A REAL BROWSER BECAUSE NOTHING IN THE APP REPO CAN ANSWER IT (jsdom performs no layout). All three overlays land FULLY INSIDE the visible viewport, at both of the iframe heights tested — 952 CSS px (viewport 1100) and 752 CSS px (viewport 900): `contribute-menu-items` at CSS y 177..286 (x 1259, w 200), `matchup-detail` at y 104..356 (x 451, w 582), `prompt-detail` at y 104..311 (x 451, w 582). Every trigger is also in view and stays put across viewport heights (`contribute-trigger` y 143..173, `grid-col-header` y 182..240, `grid-group-matchup` y 240..265). So no scroll is needed, `yFrom: appFrame` survives, and one recipe-level rect can serve all three — which is what the recipe form requires, since `crop` has no per-state override. ── ⚠️ THE ASSETS ARE LESS DIFFERENT FROM EACH OTHER THAN THE OLD THREE WERE, and that is the honest cost. All three show the SAME grid with a different overlay over it, and `grid-contribute`'s overlay is a 200x109 CSS px dropdown in the top-right — the weakest of the three as a listing image. The old set showed three genuinely different screens. 🔴 A declared rect makes the identical-box check INERT, so nothing in the pipeline will tell you if these collapse into near-duplicates; that judgement is BY EYE and it is the reason this note exists.
_noExplainerState: 🔴 There is deliberately NO `explainer` state, and it is not an oversight. Dismissing the how-to PERSISTS (it does not come back on reload), so the first state that dismisses [data-testid='howto-dismiss'] destroys it for every later state in the same run — the explainer state was tried last and captured nothing, because by then it was gone. Capturing it needs a profile that has never dismissed it, which this scripted path cannot arrange. custom-generators' recipe gets away with an `explainer` state only because it is listed FIRST. Do not 'fix' this by reordering: the three states each dismiss it as their first action, so whichever runs first still kills it.
